hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to close-up views of black, textured mechanical objects—predominantly camera lens caps—featuring bold, high-contrast text centered on their surface. The core activating visual pattern consists of bright white or metallic silver lettering (e.g., brand names like "Nikon," "Canon," or "OLYMPUS") set against a deep black or dark charcoal background characterized by a matte, stippled, or granular plastic texture. Surrounding the text, the objects typically display molded geometric details such as concentric rings, ridges, recessed grooves, or mechanical pinch-grips. The neuron is invariant to the specific text content, slight perspective changes, and background environments (which range from pitch black to denim blue, brown wood, or colorful bokeh), provided the strong light-on-dark typographic contrast and the dark industrial form are preserved. The activating object typically occupies 50–90% of the image area, with the text horizontally centered and acting as the primary focal point.
